React · Hooks

Can we call a hook conditionally? Why not?

Answer

No. React identifies hooks by their call order on each render. If a hook is skipped in one render (inside if, loop, or after an early return), all following hooks shift position and get the wrong state, causing bugs or the error "Rendered fewer hooks than expected".

Instead, call the hook unconditionally and put the condition inside it:

useEffect(() => {
  if (!userId) return;
  fetchUser(userId);
}, [userId]);

(Exception: the new use() API in React 19 can be called conditionally.)
